item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.11
item.description:
## Sounds Like, a page of its own
Finding tunes that sound alike was hidden in a tune's right-click menu. It's now the easiest way through the collection.
- **Sounds Like** in the sidebar shows the tunes across HVSC that sound most like the one playing, closest first, with how alike each is. Play them all, drift from there, or save them as a playlist. - **Find Similar** sits at the end of the selected row in every list, and **⌘L** does the same, or uses the tune playing when nothing is selected. It's on the inspector's Sounds Like card too. - **Hop from tune to tune.** Find Similar on one of the matches goes on from there. The way you came stays above the list, each tune a link back, and **Follow What's Playing** starts over from the music. - Sorting a list by how alike its tunes sound is still there, as **Sort by Likeness** in a tune's right-click menu. While a list is sorted that way, the tune it's compared to sits as a barcode over the Fingerprint column, lined up with the rows' barcodes. - In the terminal app, the tune under the cursor shows **l find similar**. Each `l` goes on from the last, the title keeps the way you came, and `Esc` goes back along it instead of quitting.
## The playback bar and the toolbar
- **Slide two fingers** sideways anywhere on the playback bar to slide its title to the tune before or after; lift them and that one plays. - **Under the Hood** moved from the playback bar to the toolbar, and its button stays tinted while the drawer is open. - **Surprise Me** and **Add Files** left the toolbar. They're in the Playback and File menus, with ⇧⌘R and ⌘O as before. - My Playlist and your playlists have a **+** before the filter, to add SID files or folders from your Mac.
## A new look for the terminal app
`resonance` in Terminal got a makeover, in the style of an old BBS.
- **Your accent color.** The terminal app now uses the accent you chose in System Settings, and only for what's chosen or playing: a ● on the tune that plays, a ❯ at the cursor, and the played part of the bar. - **Sections** sit on gray bars, with thin lines between the columns that fade out toward the bottom. - **Tidier lists.** Composer names get the room they need, lengths line up on the right, and long playlist names shorten instead of hiding their count. - **Fewer keys at the bottom**, only the ones you use most. `?` still has them all. - `i` puts the Sounds Like panel beside the list away, giving the list its room, and brings it back. - The skull fills the music page now, however far it turns or opens its jaw. - `resonance pick` lists tunes the same way.
## Scrub from the terminal
Press `t` to pick a point in the tune with the arrow keys, or jump to a tenth of it with a number, then `Enter` to go there. As in the app, the bar fills in gray to where you're going while the playhead catches up. It works on the reSIDfp and SIDLite direct engines.
## And more
- **Search Settings** from the field at the top of its sidebar. Type a setting's name, or a word like "dark mode" or "vim", and Settings goes to its page. The Settings window can be made bigger now too. - My Playlist is in the terminal app now, after Favorites. - Playlists you change in the app update in the terminal app right away, without restarting it. - A tune whose length isn't known gets a bar that sweeps across, instead of one that stays empty. - **Unplugging your headphones pauses the music**, as on iPhone, instead of playing on through the speakers. So does turning off AirPods or other Bluetooth headphones. Choosing another output yourself keeps it playing.
## Fixes
- Titles and composers with accents, such as "ö", showed as "�" in Now Playing, Control Center and the Lock Screen. Tune text is now read as Latin-1 when it isn't UTF-8, as STIL's notes already were. - HVSC's "<?>", its mark for what isn't known, no longer shows in titles and names. A tune with no known composer says **Unknown Composer**, in the app and the terminal app. "198?" years stay as they are. The collection's index is read again once, to pick this up. - The inspector's bars and envelope, the Sounds Like sphere, the Home's waves, Radial, Spectrum and the mini player's scope draw with less work for the processor, and Under the Hood's tracker and Now Playing's voice chips only redraw when what they show changes. - The MCP server for Claude and other assistants now runs in the App Sandbox. - The credits quote "All your base are belong to" correctly now, in the app and the terminal app.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.10
item.description:
## Eight new visualizers
Now Playing has room for three at a time, and you choose which in **Settings → Appearance**, from pictures of each.
- **Notes**: the tune as sheet music, with a ball hopping from note to note. - **Spectrum**: an analyzer with each voice's curve, its peaks and its notes. - **Terrain**: the last few seconds of the spectrum as a landscape. - **Ink**: each voice pours dye into dark, swirling water. - **Liquid Light**: glossy oil on a projector's glass, like a 1960s light show. - **Ferrofluid**: black liquid that stands in spikes where a voice sounds. - **Silicon**: the tune's SID in 3D with the lid off, its real die at work. - **Nimbus**: balls of cloud that merge, swell and glow with each voice.
## And more
- Playing a tune takes far less of your Mac: about 15% CPU with the window showing, down from about 47%. - Pausing, stopping, skipping, seeking and quitting fade out instead of clicking.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.9
item.description:
## Crash reports that stay on your Mac
If Resonance quits unexpectedly, it now saves a report, and Settings → Crashes lists them.
- **Nothing is sent.** A report only leaves your Mac when you copy it, save it or choose **Report on GitHub…**. - **Cleaned first.** The copy you share has your user name, your Mac's name and file paths taken out. GitHub issues are public, so read it before you post. - **Yours to delete**, one at a time or all at once.
## And more
- About Resonance has a desk now. Switch the monitor on and look around: the Credits moved there from the Help menu. - The window's columns hold still while you resize it, after a crash during a resize. - The terminal app opens straight into the player, without the logo screen.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.8
item.description:
## Simpler engine settings
Settings now offers two engines: reSIDfp, the most accurate, and SIDLite direct, the lightest. Both can scrub.
The older SIDLite and reSID engines are gone from Settings, along with Widen mono tunes, which only worked on them.
## And more
- Security updates for the libraries behind downloads and the terminal app. - The Settings sidebar is wide enough for its titles.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.7
item.description:
## A new Settings
Settings now has a sidebar of focused pages, like the one in System Settings, with Updates first.
- **Appearance:** choose Light, Dark or Auto for Resonance alone. Now Playing and Under the Hood stay dark in all three. - **Update channels:** choose Stable, Beta or Alpha in Settings → Updates. Alpha also gets betas. Your choice applies from the next release on. - **When an update fails:** Settings → Updates gives the real reason, with the details to copy for a bug report. An update that didn't install is noticed the next time Resonance opens.
## And more
- Playlists have a # column with each tune's place in the list. - A list sorted by a column has **Back to Original Order** above it, so a Top 100 keeps its ranking. - Installing the `resonance` command handles more setups: it avoids a folder where another program already has the name, tells you if your terminal may still run that program, and has a line to copy if the folder isn't on your PATH.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.6
item.description:
## A fresh start
This version is signed and notarized by Apple, so it opens like any other app, without a trip to Privacy & Security. It also runs in the App Sandbox, macOS's safe room for apps, and that means a fresh start: Resonance opens on Welcome again and doesn't see your old favourites, playlists or settings. Your earlier files are still in ~/Library/Application Support/Resonance. To keep the collection you already have, choose its HVSC folder there when Welcome asks, instead of downloading it again.
## Smart Playlists
Say what you'd like to hear, in your own words, and Resonance builds a playlist from all of HVSC by how each tune actually sounds.
## Resonance, from anywhere on your Mac
- Siri and Shortcuts: “Surprise me”, “Play something like this”, “Drift from this tune”, “Favourite this tune” and “Play Favourites”. - Spotlight finds the collection's tunes, and in Finder Space shows a SID file's title, composer and release. - The Dock icon shows a download's or scan's progress, and its menu has the controls. When Resonance is in the background, a finished download tells you. - The `resonance` command and its terminal app: playlists, search, Sounds Like, the tracker and full-screen visuals. Assistants such as Claude can use it too. Install it from Settings → Integrations. - A shared tune link now opens Resonance directly.
## And more
- Search is a place of its own: type from anywhere. - Under the Hood (⌥⌘U) slides up the tracker, registers and sweeps, every chip at once for multi-SID tunes. - Tunes outside HVSC get their length worked out, shown with a ~. - Now Playing shows the tune's fingerprint sphere. - Press ? for the keyboard shortcuts, with Vim and Emacs keys in Settings. - New credits: About Resonance → Credits.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.5
item.description:
## Scrub through a tune
Drag or click the progress bar, in the player bar, Now Playing or the menu bar player, and the tune goes there. Control Center's position slider and its 15-second skips work too.
A SID tune is a small C64 program, not a recording, so there's nothing to jump to: Resonance runs the tune to that point silently at about sixty times its speed. While it does, the bar shows where you're going in grey and the engine winding up to it, with the clock counting along; the sound comes back when it arrives, about a second per minute of tune on reSIDfp and less on SIDLite direct.
Scrubbing works on the reSIDfp and SIDLite direct engines. SIDLite and reSID play in real time only; a click on their bar says so.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.4
item.description:
## Two new sound engines
Resonance now plays through libsidplayfp, the emulator behind most SID players, rendered straight into the audio output.
- **reSIDfp** is the most accurate SID emulation available and is now the default. Tunes with filter sweeps and digi samples in particular sound closer to the real chip. - **SIDLite direct** is the same compact chip model as SIDLite, on the new player. It is the lightest on the processor of the four. - **SIDLite** and **reSID** are still there. Settings → Playback lists all four with a line on what sets each apart; changing the engine restarts the tune. - Widen mono tunes doesn't apply to the two new engines yet.
## Better Sounds Like
Sounds Like finds closer matches. In testing on composers it hadn't been tuned on, nearly twice as many of its suggestions came from the same composer as the tune you're playing.
- It now looks at how each instrument is shaped, not only which waveforms and effects a tune uses. - It also compares how tunes actually sound, using a small download made in advance. Nothing is analysed on your Mac beyond the usual scan. - Percentages in Sounds Like are worked out differently, so they won't match what you saw before. - Your fingerprints are rebuilt once: Resonance downloads the new set the first time you open it.
## Fixes
- Opening a tune from a nested composer folder, such as from Sounds Like, no longer shows an empty page with 0 tunes. It opens the folder the tune is listed under.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.3
item.description:
## Share a tune
Send a friend the tune you're listening to.
- **Share…** next to Add to… in Now Playing, the inspector and the menu bar player, and **Share** in a tune's right-click menu, makes a short link to any tune in HVSC: Copy Link, Messages, Mail, or any other app. - Pasted into Messages, Slack, Discord and the like, the link shows the tune's card: title, composer, year, length and its sound fingerprint. - A click on **Open in Resonance** opens the tune in Resonance, at the same subtune. If your collection is older and doesn't have it, Resonance offers the HVSC update; if you have no collection yet, the download. - Friends without Resonance get a page with the tune's card, its fingerprint turning, and a download link.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.2
item.description:
## Automatic updates
Resonance now keeps itself up to date.
- **Check for Updates…** in the Resonance menu looks for a new version right away. - Resonance checks once a day by itself. Turn this off, or let it download and install updates when you quit, in Settings → Advanced → Updates. - Every update is checked against Resonance's signing key before it's installed. Nothing about your Mac is sent.
This is the last version you need to download by hand.
